what: Fix (c) step 1: identity headers the Databricks Apps proxy forwards to the reviewer portal, and whether client-supplied x-forwarded-* headers survive the proxy. /whoami is read-only; no sandbox rows were written.

runner_sp.source: runner auth run 4e1c1af4-378f-4b05-be22-8bc703da75b4 (e2e_runs), both candidate token sources returned the same body

spoof_test.caller: owner conroyri@nih.gov, signed in, browser devtools
spoof_test.source: owner report in session; outgoing headers confirmed in the browser Network tab (Request Headers)

conclusions: The Apps proxy overwrites client-supplied x-forwarded-email and x-forwarded-preferred-username with the caller's authenticated identity. On this path the header is authoritative for identity.

x-forwarded-user is email-shaped for BOTH callers (<id>@<workspace id>), so a pattern match on '@' cannot tell a service principal from a person. For the SP, x-forwarded-email holds its application id (a UUID), not an email. So the control checks x-forwarded-email by exact match against an explicit approver set.
residual: INFERENCE, not a measurement: the spoof test ran on the owner's (human) path only. The runner-probe confirmation on the SP path was declined on schedule grounds. Proxy ingress handling is assumed not to vary by principal type.
not_tested: x-forwarded-user was not supplied by the client in the spoof test
the /mcp POST path was not spoof-tested; the GET /whoami path was
